DJI Matrice 30. Half the weight of the M300 on 16 in rotors and a 6S pack, against the M300's 21 in rotors and 12S. Its value here is SCALE: a model that only works at one size is not much of a model.

Validated against the published 36 min HOVER time, which DJI states separately from the 41 min flight time.

_published.battery: 2x TB30 in parallel, Li-ion 6S, 5880 mAh, 131.6 Wh, 685 g each

_inferred: Motor Kv and resistance, ESC parameters and airframe drag areas are NOT published. DJI names the motor (3511) and propeller (1671) but publishes no electrical parameters for either.
_calibration:
Nothing tuned: usable capacity at 80% as for the M300, and the rotor figure of merit at the default for 16 in (0.71). Propulsion only, the model gives 35.7 min hover against DJI's published 36.

Comparing overall hover efficiency (ideal momentum power divided by electrical power):
  M300, 21 in rotors: model 64.1%, real 69.2%
  M30,  16 in rotors: model 56.8%, real 57.3%

Real hardware loses efficiency scaling down: smaller propellers run at lower Reynolds number, and smaller motors and ESCs are less efficient too. Until audit M13 the model had no rotor figure of merit at all; it gave 47.0 min here, 31% optimistic, with the small aircraft MORE efficient than the large one. The default figure of merit now falls with diameter, through the size classes the Status check already used; it is not fitted to this aircraft.

The avionics rails below add about 72 W, which DJI does not publish; with them, as the GUI runs this file, the hover is 27.2 min. On an aircraft this size they matter, so edit them if you know the real draw.

Below about 9 in, trust the default figure of merit least: load a measured propeller table on the Propeller tab, or enter a measured figure of merit, and the default is bypassed.
